What is MDM Font Management and why does listing copy matter?

Font Management covers MDM and Configuration Profile Font payloads that install and manage organization fonts on enrolled Macs, iPhones, and iPads — managed fonts in Font Book and system font lists. Marketing those workflows on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

How is this different from Configuration Profiles?

Font Management listing copy markets organization font install and managed typography on enrolled fleet devices. Configuration Profile listing copy markets installable .mobileconfig payload file distribution for Wi-Fi, VPN, certificates, and broad settings catalogs. Font payload may ride inside a profile, but profile distribution is not the Font Management lead. Listing vocabulary must follow your English lead feature.

How is this different from Managed Apps, Content Caching, or Volume Purchase?

Font Management governs organization font deployment. Managed Apps govern app install and Managed App Configuration. Content Caching governs macOS bandwidth savings. Volume Purchase governs VPP app licensing. Each is a separate Apple MDM or org surface — do not reuse boilerplate across them.

How is this different from Kernel Extensions, Gatekeeper, or USB Restrictions?

Font Management installs and manages organization typography assets. Kernel Extensions govern legacy kext loading. Gatekeeper controls software source and notarization trust. USB Restrictions govern peripheral connection policy. Do not lead Font Management pages with kext, Gatekeeper, or USB restriction marketing unless your English source genuinely shows those on separate frames.
